archetype.name: Lottery Team (shooting collapse)
archetype.definition: A team whose point differential and record both sit near the bottom of the league, here because a high-volume three-point offense has stopped making shots while its best shooter is sidelined.

report.headline: Last year's fifth-best offense is now the league's worst, and the record shows it
report.take:
Charlotte arrived as a team on the way up. Last season it went 44-38 with the league's fifth-best offense (119.4 ORtg), and it would have finished better if not for a W vs Pt Diff of -9. Fifteen games into this one it is 4-11, 28th of 30 on the site, with a Net Rtg of -11. This is not bad luck in close games: W vs Pt Diff is +1 and the margin implies 3 wins, so the record is, if anything, slightly flattering. At this rate the season ends around 22 wins.

The whole drop is on offense. The ORtg has fallen to 104.4, last in the league and 9.9 points below average. The shot profile hasn't changed much. The Hornets still take more threes than anyone (51.9% 3PA Rate, 1st), as they did last season, but they are hitting 31% from three, last in the league, after 37.8% a year ago. Around that they are also last in TS %, FT Rate and TOV %. The context matters: Grayson Allen, the one high-efficiency scorer (67.8 TS % on 21.2 USG %), is out, as are Dennis Schröder and Grant Williams. The shots have gone to Brandon Miller (31.9 USG %, 47.5 TS %) and Naz Reid (28 USG %, 47.7 TS %), and both are converting them poorly.

The overall numbers hide that the rest of the team is not broken. Charlotte leads the league in ORB %, DRB % and REB %, and that rebounding carries over from last season (54 REB % then, 54.1 now), so it is real. The defense is 17th by DRtg, close to average, even though opponents are shooting 40% from three against it, the worst mark in the league. That number is mostly noise: the Hornets defend the rim respectably (12th in Opp Rim FG %) and hold opposing centers to the fewest points in the league. Bigs like Ryan Kalkbrenner (75.5 TS %, +15.4 On-Off) and Moussa Diabaté (65.7 TS %) are doing their jobs.

The recent trend is mixed. The record slid from 3-4 in October to 1-7 in November, and the last ten games went 1-9. The last five, though, were much closer (-3.8 a game, 6.73 better than the season rate), and they included a five-point loss at Phoenix and an overtime loss to the Lakers. The defense and rebounding are holding steady. Whether the season turns depends on the three-point shooting coming back toward normal and on Allen's return.

strengths.title: Owns the glass at both ends
strengths.body: Charlotte leads the league in offensive, defensive and total rebounding percentage, well above the league average at each. It is not a fluke: last season's REB % was 54 as well, and the center rotation of Reid, Diabaté and Kalkbrenner gives it size for the full game. It is also the main thing keeping a broken offense alive, because second chances make up for some of the misses.

strengths.title: Efficient, rim-anchoring center rotation
strengths.body: The bigs who don't take threes are the team's most efficient players: Kalkbrenner at 75.5 TS % with a +15.4 On-Off, and Diabaté at 65.7 TS % with a team-high 1.1 Win Shares. On defense, opposing centers score fewer points against Charlotte than against any other team. That production depends on role rather than on hot shooting, so it should last.

strengths.title: Defense better than its results
strengths.body: A 115.4 DRtg ranks 17th even though opponents are shooting 40% from three, 4.6 points above the league. Rim defense is solid (12th in Opp Rim FG %). Opponent three-point shooting is the least stable defensive number, so the defensive rating should improve as it comes back down.

concerns.title: Three-point volume without makes
concerns.body: No team relies on the three more, and no team makes it at a lower rate. That combination is why the ORtg has fallen from 119.4 last season to 104.4, the worst in the league. Some recovery is likely, since this group hit 37.8% on similar volume a year ago, but most of that shooting came from Allen, who is out.

concerns.title: Usage in the wrong hands
concerns.body: With Allen out, the shots have gone to Miller and Reid, and both are below 48 TS % while using the most possessions on the team. Reid's -7.2 On-Off suggests his high-volume shooting hurts more than it helps. Until Allen returns or Miller's shot recovers, the half-court offense has no efficient creator.

concerns.title: Turnovers and no free throws
concerns.body: Charlotte is last in TOV % and last in FT Rate, and both are well off the league average. These problems have nothing to do with shooting luck. The guards are turning the ball over and nobody is getting to the line, and the F-graded backcourt suggests that won't fix itself.

trend.note: A 3-4 October became a 1-7 November and a 1-9 run over the last ten. The last five games were far more competitive, though, with the margin 6.73 points better than the season rate.

weekAhead.headline: Four home games, three against fellow strugglers: a real window
weekAhead.body:
This is the softest week the Hornets are likely to get. All four games are in Charlotte, and three of them come against teams ranked 21st or lower on the site. Even so, the Hornets' -11 Net Rtg is worse than Chicago's, Brooklyn's and Washington's, so this is a chance to win games rather than a run of expected wins. They have already lost to both Brooklyn (104-114) and Washington (79-95).

Memphis opens the week and is the hardest matchup possible for this offense. The Grizzlies have the second-best ORtg, the league's best 3P %, and the best opponent 3P % on defense. Chicago and Brooklyn are the games to win: both rank among the league's worst defenses, Chicago gives up the most rim attempts and rebounds poorly on its own glass, and Brooklyn allows a 56.4 Opp eFG %. Washington closes the week and defends the three well, but it is weak on the boards at both ends, which suits Charlotte's strength.

keyMatchups.title: Memphis's perimeter defense vs. volume shooting
keyMatchups.body: Memphis holds opponents to 32.5% from three, the best in the league, and Charlotte takes more threes than anyone. The Grizzlies also shoot 39.1% themselves. Without its threes falling, Charlotte's best chance is to keep the Grizzlies off the offensive glass and win the rebounding margin by a lot.

keyMatchups.title: Charlotte's bigs against Chicago's soft interior
keyMatchups.body: Chicago ranks 28th in DRtg and 28th in DRB %, and it allows the highest share of opponent shots at the rim. That suits Diabaté and Kalkbrenner, who score efficiently close to the basket and on putbacks. If the Hornets can't win this game at home, the problem goes deeper than shooting.

keyMatchups.title: Rematches with Brooklyn and Washington
keyMatchups.body: Both earlier games were losses, the Washington one a 79-point performance on offense. Brooklyn's defense is porous (27th in Opp eFG %), so the shooting has a chance to recover. Washington guards the three well but ranks 27th in ORB %, so Charlotte's rebounding edge should be at its largest that night.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the 31% three-point shooting starts moving toward last season's level against the Chicago and Brooklyn defenses, and who takes the shots while Allen is out and Miller is day-to-day.

restOfSeason.body:
At the current rate the season ends around 22 wins, and the margin supports that record, so no luck correction is coming from close games. Some correction should come from shooting. Opponents won't keep hitting 40% from three against a defense that is otherwise around average, and a team that shot 37.8% on heavy volume last season shouldn't stay at 31%. The rebounding and the center rotation are real and should hold. The turnovers and the lack of free throws look structural.

The realistic outcome is a team that plays closer to its last five games than its first ten: still losing more than it wins, but by smaller margins. That points to a finish in the mid-to-high 20s in wins. Allen's return is the biggest swing factor; without him, the offense has no efficient high-usage scorer. A play-in push would need both full shooting recovery and a healthy backcourt, and the sheet gives no sign of either yet.
swingFactors: Brandon Miller's shooting efficiency on heavy usage
Opponent three-point shooting coming back to the league average

confidence.note: Fifteen games, several rotation players out, and three-point percentages that are still unstable at both ends.
